questions.q: Why use median and MAD instead of mean and standard deviation for the baseline?
options: Outliers do not distort them, so the anomalies you search for do not hide themselves
They work only for normal data

questions.q: Residuals have MAD = 5. A new residual is −30. What is the robust z-score (use 0.6745)?
questions.why: z = 0.6745 × (−30) / 5 = −4.047. A negative z is a dip.

questions.q: Which are ways to reduce alert fatigue? (pick all)
options: Require the anomaly to last several points

questions.q: Scenario: a metric that is always near 0 and sometimes 1 (rare errors). A z-score detector fires on every 1. What is a better approach?
options: Treat it as a count: use a rate/Poisson-type test over a longer window
why: Correct: sparse counts need a count-based test or aggregation.
It may be an important error counter.
MAPE is a forecast metric and breaks near zero.

questions.q: Scenario: the metric feed stops for 20 minutes but the detector shows no alert. What was missing?
why: No model can score data that does not arrive.
Correct: silence can be the loudest anomaly.

questions.q: Scenario: 1 000 000 points per day are checked, 0.1% are truly bad, and the detector flags 1% with 80% recall. About how many true anomalies are caught?
questions.why: True anomalies = 1 000 000 × 0.001 = 1 000. Recall 0.8 gives 800 caught. The 10 000 flags mean precision is only 8%.
